_help: Decision policy for the customer-support persona (Lumen Cloud). Every threshold carries a one-sentence why.
on_ezio_failure_why: Fail closed but recoverable: an email we could not verify waits for a human instead of going out, and HOLD rather than BLOCK because the draft itself may be fine.
tier_decisions_why: The tier is a blended score that can look fine while a fact is wrong (score traps) or look poor on harmless drafts, so our own price and policy checks decide facts; a RED tier alone only sends the draft to a human.

tone.why: Customer emails must stay professional; a tone score below 40 signals hype or hostility a manager should see.

bias.why: A strongly one-sided message to a customer is a reputational risk worth a second look.

agreement.why: Very low agreement suggests the reply goes along with a customer's mistaken premise, which the rules send to review.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Most support emails make no public-knowledge claims and our own data checks still run, so a missing accuracy score is not a reason to hold (business rule 5).
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: When Ezio's fact-check is down we cannot verify public claims such as legal statements, so the draft waits for a human rather than going out unchecked.
